sources.title: FY26 Program Report
sources.summary: Harborlight's FY26 program report covers its adult learning work. It enrolled 1,148 adult learners, up from 936, and 71 earned a high school equivalency credential. Staff recommend the board approve a $1,610,000 FY2027 budget to add a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library.

sources.title: Harborlight Brand Guide 2025
sources.summary: Version 2.1 of the Harborlight Brand Guide came out in March 2025. It sets the rules for the group's name, colors, fonts, voice and logo (p. 1, p. 2, p. 3). For example, it calls for "adult learners," bans words like "at-risk," and requires a 501(c)(3) line at the end of every printed piece (p. 3).

passages.text:
In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites, up from 936 the year before. Of those learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential and 389 were English language learners.
Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in the organization's history.
A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight employs 11 full-time staff, including four site coordinators.

Operating expenses for FY2026 were $1,420,000. Program costs were 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants provided $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000.
The cost per learner was $1,237.
At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist, most of them at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks.

Staff recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators. Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year and cut the waitlist in half.
“I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring,” said a learner at the Riverside site.
Present: board chair Lorraine Okafor, treasurer Dev Patel, executive director Marcus Bell, communications director Denise Alvarez, six board members.

The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's target of 4 months.
The board asked staff to bring a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request to the October 21 board meeting.
Board members asked for a short deck they can use with funders when they talk about the sixth site.
The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

Harborlight Brand Guide
Version 2.1, March 2025. Prepared by a volunteer designer.
Use this guide for everything Harborlight prints, posts or sends.
Our name: always 'Harborlight Literacy Project' on first use, 'Harborlight' after.
Never 'HLP' in public materials.

Color
Harbor Teal
HEX #0E5E6F PMS 3155 C CMYK 100 / 30 / 30 / 40
Primary. Headlines, the logo, bands.
Sunrise Gold
HEX #F2A900 PMS 130 C CMYK 0 / 30 / 100 / 0
Accent. Use sparingly: rules, callouts, one number.
Lighthouse Red
HEX #C0392B PMS 7621 C CMYK 10 / 90 / 90 / 5
Calls to action only.
Warm Gray
HEX #5B5651 PMS Warm Gray 11 C CMYK 0 / 10 / 15 / 70
Secondary text.
Paper
HEX #FAF7F2 
Backgrounds.
Ink
HEX #2B2B2B 
Body text.

Type
Headlines: Montserrat Bold or ExtraBold. Sentence case.
Body: Lora Regular, 10 to 12 point. Italic for quotes.
If Montserrat is not installed, use Arial Bold. If Lora is not installed, use Georgia.
Voice: warm, hopeful, plain. Talk about learners, not 'clients' or 'beneficiaries'.
Never say: illiterate, less fortunate, underprivileged, at-risk.
Say 'adult learners', not 'students'.
Every printed piece ends with: Harborlight Literacy Project is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. EIN 47-1928361.
Logo: teal lighthouse mark with wordmark. Clear space equal to the height of the H.

chats.content: Reserves are 3.2 months, short of the 4-month target. Spending would rise $190,000, from $1,420,000 to $1,610,000. How will the board fund this without draining reserves further?

The sources don't say how the board will pay for the larger budget or protect reserves, because neither one includes an FY2027 revenue or funding plan.
Here is what the sources do say. Treasurer Dev Patel reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's target of 4 months [P8]. FY2026 operating expenses were $1,420,000 [P3]. Staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which adds a sixth site and two site coordinators [P5].
In FY2026, foundation grants provided $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000 [P3]. The sources don't say whether any of these will grow.
Board members asked for a short deck to use with funders about the sixth site [P8]. That suggests they plan to raise money from funders, but the notes give no goals or amounts [P8]. The board planned to vote on the budget on October 21. The sources don't record the outcome [P8].
chats.followups: ["How many more learners would the sixth site serve each year?", "Which sites have the most adults on the waitlist?", "What did the board ask staff to bring on October 21?"]

chats.content:
The sources give few facts about the Riverside site, except that it and Eastgate hold most of the 287 adults on the year-end waitlist [P4].
The average wait at year end was nine weeks [P4]. The sources don't split the waitlist by site, so the number for Riverside alone is unknown [P4].
The proposed sixth site would open at the Eastgate branch library, not at Riverside [P5]. Staff estimate it would serve 180 more learners a year and cut the waitlist in half [P5]. The sources don't say how much of that help would reach people waiting for Riverside.
A learner at Riverside said, "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring" [P5].
The sources don't give Riverside's enrollment, costs, staff or learning results.
chats.followups: ["How many site coordinators does Harborlight employ across its sites?", "How long did learners wait on the waitlist at year end?", "How many more learners would the Eastgate sixth site serve?"]

guide.text: These sources are Harborlight's FY26 program report and notes from a board retreat on September 13.
Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in fiscal year 2026, up from 936 the year before.
Still, 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, and the average wait was nine weeks.
Staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 that adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators.
Reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's target of 4 months, and the board votes on October 21.

settings.case_of:o_f2dc8ef2cc88: Funders who could back Harborlight's sixth site will read this deck with board members. They must come away believing that need is outgrowing our five sites, and that a sixth site at Eastgate is a sound, proven way to meet it. The strongest evidence is enrollment growth from 936 to 1,148 learners, 287 adults on the waitlist at year end, 68 percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gaining a reading level, and a cost per learner of $1,237. They will ask whether the work works, who does it, what the new site adds and what it costs. The ask is the $190,000 increase from $1,420,000 in FY2026 spending to a $1,610,000 FY2027 budget, which opens a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library with two site coordinators.
